value: This article evaluates the incidental predictions made by Robin Hanson and Eliezer Yudkowsky during their 2008-2013 "FOOM Debate" on recursive AI self-improvement. By analyzing their forecasts on topics such as AI architecture standardization, the relative importance of compute versus algorithms, and the utility of human-accumulated knowledge, the author concludes that Hanson's predictions generally aligned better with subsequent AI developments, though Yudkowsky was notably accurate regarding Cyc's unpromising nature. The analysis yields meta-level insights, supporting Hanson's methodology of leveraging abstractions with proven prior predictive power and emphasizing the necessity of providing specific, verifiable predictions when asserting a strong track record.
